title: Inference Unit Economics Intake - QuartzMart Checkout
summary: Introductory discovery focused on QuartzMart's checkout AI use case and tight budget/latency constraints. Discussed per-token pricing sensitivity, tradeoffs between Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private, batching and KV cache strategies, and a pilot plan to run benchmarks. Action items: Redwood to send pilot pricing and runbook; QuartzMart to provide sample workload and security contacts.
transcript:
Header: 2026-09-03 16:00 UTC — Duration 44m — Recorded via Zoom. Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ortega (Redwood) — Samir Patel, Lena Ortiz, Marcus Nguyen (QuartzMart).

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Diego's our systems SE and he'll cover benchmarks. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Samir Patel: Good, thanks. Quick context — we run personalized checkout suggestions, pretty short prompts, typical response ~120 tokens but sometimes up to 400 for cart-level summarizations. Latency target for 90th pctl is 250ms. Budget's tight, we have a monthly cap for inference of about $35k.
[00:22] Diego Ortega: Got it. Quick question — are you currently using any hosted LLM API or self-hosting?
[00:26] Lena Ortiz: We have a mixed approach. Most is OpenAI for prototyping, but production is on-prem with a handful of 8-GPU boxes, running smaller distill models. We don't have a solid batching pipeline yet.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Okay, that helps. High level — we typically evaluate three deployment flavors: Redwood Hosted (fastest start), Dedicated reserved pools (predictable throughput), and Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency and stricter controls. Each has different unit-econ levers.
[00:52] Marcus Nguyen: Cost is the primary constraint. We can relax latency a bit if it materially saves dollars. But for checkout we can't go past 400ms p90 without hurting conversion.
[01:02] Samir Patel: Also important: we need audit logs and KMS integration. SOC2 is a must.
[01:07] Maya Chen: Understood. We have SOC2 and KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated; Hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys in some regions. We'll send the SOC2 and KMS doc after this.
[01:17] Diego Ortega: If I can jump to the unit economics levers — there are a few: per-token price, batching size, kv cache/prefix caching, quantized model variants, and fallback routing. For short prompts, batching gives less theoretical gain but if you can tolerate 50–100ms extra wait for batching windows, you can increase throughput and lower per-token cost.
[01:36] Lena Ortiz: Hmm, so batching would add tail latency, right? We're sensitive to p90.
[01:40] Diego Ortega: Right. That's why we tune batching windows and use latency-aware routing. Also prefix KV caching can cut cost dramatically if you have repeated prompt prefixes (e.g., site header, product context). It saves compute for cached tokens. We can estimate cost reduction after seeing actual duplicate rates.
[01:55] Samir Patel: Our prompts have a lot of repeated context — product metadata + user history — so cache hit rate could be decent. Do you have numbers on caching savings?
[02:03] Diego Ortega: Ballpark: 30–60% token compute savings for high prefix reuse; for your 120-token typical response that could be meaningful. But depends on model size and KV cache effectiveness.
[02:11] Maya Chen: On pricing: for hosted we quote per-token list rates; Dedicated transitions to a mixed model — reserved capacity plus lower per-token variable — and Private is typically license + infra. We can give a pilot pricing matrix so you can compare expected spend against your traffic.
[02:27] Marcus Nguyen: Can we get an example run for our volume? We do ~2M requests/month now, expected to grow 3x in six months.
[02:34] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll provide a worked example. If you send current qps distribution and sample payloads, we can produce a per-token spend estimate with scenarios (hosted vs dedicated).
[02:42] Samir Patel: We'll share a 7-day sample of traffic. Who should we send that to?
[02:46] Maya Chen: Send to maya@redwood.ai and diego@redwood.ai. We'll treat it as sample data; we have an NDA template if you need it.
[02:52] Lena Ortiz: Security question — for Private, do we still get Redwood Console telemetry? We need control of logs in-house.
[02:58] Diego Ortega: In Private, the control plane is customer-managed; you can choose log retention and have audit logs sent to your SIEM. For Dedicated we keep a thin control plane but can push logs to your cloud project.
[03:09] Samir Patel: Good. Another thing: we saw Redwood mentions intelligent batching/caching recommendations. How automated is that?
[03:15] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize surfaces suggestions based on your workload — recommended batch sizes, cache TTLs, quantization profiles. For pilots we often run a quick analysis on sample prompts and return a config that balances latency and cost.
[03:27] Marcus Nguyen: About quantization — are there accuracy regressions we should expect? Checkout content has a lot of entity names and numbers.
[03:33] Diego Ortega: There's always a slight quality delta for extreme quantization. We recommend running targeted evals on your prompt set. In practice, 4-bit or mixed-precision modes maintain quality for many tasks; we can show regressions by prompt category.
[03:47] Samir Patel: Ok so pilot plan would be: run a small batch of our samples through hosted and dedicated variants, measure cost/latency/quality, and recommend configuration?
[03:56] Maya Chen: Exactly. Typical pilot: 2 weeks of benchmarking, Redwood provides runbook + scripts, we run through Redwood Hosted and a Dedicated-reserved pool with the same model family, we track p50/p90/p99, tokens, and cost. Attainable next step would be scheduling the benchmark slot.
[04:10] Lena Ortiz: How disruptive is a Dedicated pilot to our infra?
[04:13] Diego Ortega: Minimal — Dedicated can be spun in our cloud with network peering. If you want on-premdedicated, that'll need some coordination but we can start with Hosted vs cloud Dedicated first.
[04:23] Samir Patel: Any expectations on credit for the pilot?
[04:26] Maya Chen: We usually provide pilot credits for Hosted. For Dedicated we can offer a time-limited discount on reserved capacity during the evaluation. We'll include pilot credit details in the pricing doc.
[04:36] Marcus Nguyen: One more constraint — we must be able to fail open to a cheaper model if cost spikes. Do you support automatic fallback by policy?
[04:43] Diego Ortega: Yes, our smart routing supports fallbacks to cheaper variants or different regions when thresholds hit. You can define per-route policies.
[04:50] (unclear) Speaker 1: mm-hmm.
[04:52] Maya Chen: Quick qualification — who will be decision owners and timeline?
[04:55] Marcus Nguyen: I'm the technical sponsor; Samir owns evaluation; finance will sign off if the pilot shows runway. We want a decision within six weeks if results are promising.
[05:04] Samir Patel: Also need to confirm SSO integration for our admin — SAML.
[05:09] Maya Chen: We support SAML/SSO for Console. We'll attach the SSO integration guide.
[05:14] Diego Ortega: I'll note the specific metrics we'll collect for the benchmark: per-request token counts, model latency per stage, batching latency windows, cache hit rate, and cost-per-token effective after caching.
[05:27] Lena Ortiz: For sample workload — do you need raw user data? We can provide anonymized JSON, is that OK?
[05:32] Maya Chen: Yes anonymized is fine. If you prefer, we can run synthetic traffic that matches your token distribution; sample is preferable though.
[05:40] Samir Patel: Great. A few quick objections from finance thinking loud — why wouldn't we just stick with our on-prem boxes and avoid vendor lock?
[05:48] Maya Chen: Fair point. Tradeoffs: on-prem saves vendor fees but increases ops overhead, you need to manage scale spikes, and there's engineering maintenance costs for optimizations (batching, kernel tuning). Redwood aims to lower unit ops cost and give predictable SLAs. We can put economics side-by-side for a 12-month TCO comparison.
[06:07] Marcus Nguyen: Can you support model pinning so we can freeze a version for compliance?
[06:11] Diego Ortega: Yes, both Dedicated and Private allow model version pinning and rollout controls.
[06:15] Maya Chen: Okay moving to wrap up — I'll recap next steps.
[06:20] Maya Chen: Action items: Maya/Diego send pilot pricing spreadsheet, benchmark runbook, SOC2/KMS/SSO docs. QuartzMart to send 7-day sample anonymized workload and confirm decision committee. Schedule benchmark kickoff for next week if possible.
[06:33] Samir Patel: Sounds good. One last stray note — we sometimes do cost allocation by product so the ability to tag routes and produce per-route cost is important.
[06:41] Diego Ortega: Redwood Console has per-route and token-level breakdowns; we can demonstrate in the pilot.
[06:48] Marcus Nguyen: Alright, let's aim for kickoff the week of Sep 7.
[06:52] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite.
[06:57] (call end)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional speaker swaps and a few misheard technical terms (KV cache transcribed as KV cash).
